Kitchen Installation Near Me Cost: UK Guide

30 July 2026·BMB Renovation

If you have searched for “kitchen installation near me cost”, you are probably trying to work out whether a quote is reasonable before committing to a fitter. The answer depends on much more than the size of the room. Your choice of units, worktops and appliances, the condition of the walls and floor, and whether plumbing or electrics need moving can all change the final figure. This guide explains the rough costs you may encounter in the UK, what a local kitchen fitter may include, and the questions to ask when comparing quotes in Watford, Hertfordshire, North London or Bedfordshire.

How much does kitchen installation cost in the UK?

As a rough typical UK guide, installation-only labour for a straightforward kitchen may be around £2,000 to £5,000, although smaller jobs may cost less and complex installations may cost considerably more. This may assume that the kitchen has already been designed and supplied, the room is in reasonable condition, and the existing layout is not changing substantially. The scope can include removing old units, installing cabinets and worktops, fitting appliances, and associated plumbing, electrical or finishing work, but this must be confirmed in writing. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

For a complete new kitchen, including units, worktops, appliances, installation and some preparation work, a broad typical UK working budget may be approximately £8,000 to £20,000 or more. A basic, compact kitchen with standard units and limited alterations may fall towards the lower end. A larger kitchen with bespoke cabinetry, stone worktops, premium appliances, structural changes or extensive rewiring may exceed this range. These are rough guide prices only: every project differs, and you should get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

What does a local kitchen fitter usually include?

The phrase “kitchen installation” is not used consistently by every contractor. One quote may include only cabinet assembly and fitting, while another may cover the whole project from removal through to final decoration. Before comparing prices, ask each fitter to state exactly what is included and what will be arranged by you or another trade.

  • Removal and disposal of the existing kitchen, including whether skip hire or waste charges are included.
  • Assembly, levelling and fixing of base units, wall units, tall units, panels, plinths and end pieces.
  • Worktop cutting and fitting, with separate pricing often applying to laminate, solid wood, quartz, granite or other specialist surfaces.
  • Sink, tap and appliance connections, subject to the required plumbing, electrical supply and manufacturer instructions.
  • Plumbing alterations, such as moving a sink, dishwasher or washing machine, if this is part of the contractor’s scope.
  • Electrical work, including additional sockets, lighting or appliance connections where appropriate and agreed in advance.
  • Wall and floor preparation, tiling, flooring, decorating and making good, which may be included, priced separately or excluded.
  • Final adjustments, silicone sealing and removal of protective materials once the installation is complete.

The main factors that affect kitchen installation prices

The number of cabinets is only one part of the calculation. Labour may increase when the room requires more trades, more detailed preparation or more time-consuming finishing work. A local team that handles several parts of the installation in-house can sometimes make coordination simpler, but you should still check the detailed scope rather than assuming that every trade is included.

Layout, access and preparation

Keeping the sink, cooker and dishwasher in their current positions can reduce plumbing and electrical alterations. Moving them may improve the design, but it can involve new pipework, cables, waste connections, floor repairs and wall making-good. Removing a wall, widening a doorway or altering a window can introduce structural work and may require separate professional advice. Uneven floors, damaged plaster, damp, old wiring or poor ventilation can also add preparation costs.

Materials, appliances and finish level

Cabinet construction, door style and internal storage fittings can create significant differences in price. Standard laminate worktops are often less costly than solid timber, compact surfaces or natural stone, while bespoke sizes and complicated joints can increase fitting time. Integrated appliances, boiling-water taps, filtered-water systems, feature lighting and specialist extraction can all require additional installation work. If you are supplying your own appliances, check their dimensions and connection requirements before ordering the units.

The condition and age of the property

Older homes in and around Watford, Bushey, St Albans, Harrow, Luton and Bedford may have walls, floors, plumbing or electrics that need attention before a new kitchen can be fitted. This is not necessarily a problem, but it is a reason to allow a contingency rather than using every pound of the initial budget. A useful approach is to ask what the quotation assumes about the existing room and what would happen if concealed defects are discovered after removal.

How to compare kitchen installation quotes

The cheapest quote is not automatically the best value, particularly if important tasks have been left out. Request itemised quotations from two or more suitable local installers and give each of them the same plans, product list and specification. If your project is in Watford, you can review the scope of a local service such as kitchen fitting in Watford, but the same questions apply wherever you are based.

  • Check whether the price is for labour only, installation plus materials, or a complete supply-and-fit package.
  • Confirm whether VAT is included and whether the quote is fixed, estimated or subject to measured quantities.
  • Look for a clear list of included and excluded work, including demolition, waste disposal, flooring, tiling, decorating and appliance connections.
  • Ask who is responsible for supplying units, worktops, sinks, taps, appliances and finishing materials, and who checks that deliveries are complete and undamaged.
  • Confirm the expected start date, approximate duration, payment stages and how variations will be approved.
  • Ask how unexpected work is priced. Any change should be explained and agreed before the additional work is carried out.
  • Check that plumbing, tiling, electrical work and cabinet installation are covered by the named contractor or clearly allocated to other trades.
  • Make sure the final quote reflects your actual room measurements and appliance models rather than being based only on an online design.

Choosing a kitchen installation team near you

A nearby fitter may be easier to contact during a project, but location alone should not decide your choice. Look for a clear written scope, sensible answers about preparation and evidence that the contractor understands the type of kitchen you want. Ask whether the same team can coordinate cabinet fitting, plumbing, tiling, electrics and finishing work, or whether you will need to manage several separate appointments. Questions to ask before booking

Before accepting a quotation, ask for the proposed sequence of work and find out when the kitchen will be usable again. Confirm what you need to do before the start date, such as clearing cupboards, arranging appliance deliveries or protecting adjoining rooms. It is also sensible to ask how long the quote remains valid, whether design changes will affect the price, and how snagging or adjustments will be dealt with at the end. A written quotation should leave you with a realistic understanding of the total project cost, not just an attractive starting figure.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to have a kitchen installed near me?+
As a rough typical UK guide, installation-only labour may be around £2,000 to £5,000, while a complete kitchen project may be around £8,000 to £20,000 or more. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
Does kitchen installation include plumbing and electrics?+
Sometimes, but not always. Some fitters include basic connections while others charge separately or arrange for other trades. Check the quote for plumbing, electrical alterations, lighting and appliance connections.
Is it cheaper to buy a kitchen separately and pay a fitter?+
It can be, but the overall cost and result depend on delivery, measurements, missing parts and the installation scope. A supply-and-fit quote may be easier to compare, while separate supply gives you more control over product choices.
How long does a kitchen installation take?+
A straightforward replacement may take around one to two weeks, but this is only a rough guide. Structural changes, re-plumbing, rewiring, bespoke worktops, delayed deliveries and remedial work can extend the programme.
What should I check in a kitchen fitting quote?+
Check the total price, VAT, payment stages, timescale, waste removal, preparation, worktops, appliances, plumbing, electrics, tiling, flooring, decorating, exclusions and the process for agreeing variations.
